criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Mission concept, users, and national need for Great Barrier Reef monitoring are clearly defined and referenced. Technical specifications and quantitative requirements could be more thoroughly detailed.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching
Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A Gantt chart is included and mapped out. However, the plan lacks risk/contingency considerations, planned future information sources are not listed, and orbital physics logic is flawed.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.
My current choice is a geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: No actual preliminary mission design results, hand calculations, or STK outputs are presented beyond completing general tutorials.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report is clearly structured, readable, and includes a well-formatted Gantt chart. However, footnotes are raw URLs without full bibliographic details, and figures lack formal captions.

technical_issues.issue: A geostationary orbit cannot physically exist at an altitude of 600 km (geostationary altitude is ~35,786 km above the equator). A 600 km orbit is Low Earth Orbit (LEO) with a ~96-minute period.

overall: Good mission rationale for Australia. However, preliminary technical work is missing, planned information sources are absent, and asserting a 600 km geostationary orbit represents a major orbital mechanics error.

feedback.summary: You established a strong, well-justified mission rationale in the 'Mission Concept & Rationale' section addressing Australian reef monitoring. To progress to higher rubric bands, you need to rectify a major orbital mechanics error, incorporate contingency planning and explicit information sources into your project plan, present actual preliminary mission engineering calculations or simulation outputs, and standardise your referencing and figure captions.
next_steps: Correct your orbital design in 'Project Plan & Preliminary Progress': recalculate parameters recognising that geostationary orbit is ~35,786 km at the equator, whereas a 600 km altitude represents Low Earth Orbit.
Produce tangible preliminary engineering results (such as initial orbital propagation, coverage analyses, or payload hand calculations) rather than citing tutorial completions.

Upgrade report formatting by replacing raw URL footnotes with complete bibliographic citations, adding formal captions to figures, and incorporating schedule contingencies and future information sources into your plan.

criteria.C1: You clearly defined mission goals and demonstrated strong relevance to Australian conservation users. To reach the top of Accomplished, provide more detailed quantitative mission requirements and explicit technical specifications alongside your functional narrative.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart effectively outlines tasks, achieving Adequate. To reach Accomplished, correct the orbital mechanics logic (a 600 km orbit cannot be geostationary), identify planned literature and data sources, and incorporate explicit project variations and contingency management.
criteria.C3: Listing completed STK tutorials shows preliminary effort but does not supply mission-specific results. To reach Adequate or Accomplished, calculate and display actual technical progress, such as baseline orbital trades, access times, or preliminary sizing data.
criteria.C4: Your document uses a readable, logical structure. To reach Accomplished, ensure all figures include formal descriptive captions and replace raw URL footnotes with fully detailed, consistently formatted academic references.
